anti_bot_protection_assessment.question: Does the extractor now reject obvious anti-bot/challenge content generally, or was the PEI fix narrowly scoped to PEI only?
anti_bot_protection_assessment.answer: PARTIALLY GENERALIZED — the fix is architecturally generic (not hardcoded to PEI, not gated by jurisdiction ID, not keyed to any PEI-specific string), but it only covers ONE of the TWO code paths used to fetch Canadian leader profiles.

details.path: Generic path — engine/lib/subnational-leader-profile-extract.cjs, used via fetchGenericOfficialLeaderProfile() for every Canadian jurisdiction NOT in PILOT_IDS.
details.evidence: Confirmed via direct code read: looksLikeBotChallengePage() is called unconditionally at the top of extractProfileFromHtml() (returns ok:false for any jurisdiction's HTML if it matches), and extractBio() independently rejects any candidate bio text matching the same BOT_CHALLENGE_PAGE_RE pattern, again with no jurisdiction-specific gating. Tested directly against the real captured PEI Radware page (returns ok:false) and a synthetic clean profile page (still extracts correctly) in the fix's original task.

details.path: Pilot path — engine/lib/subnational-leader-profile-pilot.cjs, used for jurisdictions in PILOT_IDS (Canadian member: CA-ON only).
details.evidence: Confirmed via direct grep: zero occurrences of 'radware', 'verifying your browser', 'BOT_CHALLENGE', or 'looksLikeBotChallenge' anywhere in subnational-leader-profile-pilot.cjs. fetchCaOn() applies no content validation of any kind to premierHtml, bioHtml, or partyHtml before extracting from them. Its risk profile is DIFFERENT from the generic path's pre-fix vulnerability, not absent: leader_name is hardcoded (not derived from content at all, so bot-challenge text couldn't replace it, but a real leadership change also couldn't be detected), and the bio-extraction regex is narrowly fitted to one specific known string, making accidental contamination by generic challenge-page boilerplate unlikely in practice even without an explicit guard — but not impossible, and not defended against.

details.path: Federal PM path — src/App.js fetchMemberBio() reading the 'member_bios' Firestore collection.
details.evidence: This is not part of the subnational-leader-profile-*.cjs pipeline at all. No local engine script was found that populates member_bios for 'Mark Carney'. No validation code of any kind was found for this path. Whether it is vulnerable to the same contamination class is unknown — it may not even use an HTML-scraping mechanism at all.

generalized_validation_rule_proposal.note: Proposed only — not implemented, no code changed, no fetch or overwrite performed in this task.
proposal: 1. Move BOT_CHALLENGE_PAGE_RE and a looksLikeBotChallengePage(html) helper into the shared module (engine/lib/subnational-leader-profile-shared.cjs) so both the generic extractor and the pilot module can import the same single source of truth, instead of the check living only inside the generic extractor file.

2. In engine/lib/subnational-leader-profile-pilot.cjs's fetchCaOn() (and, if ever revisited, the other PILOT_IDS fetchers — out of scope here per the US/UK/Australia exclusion), check each fetched HTML (premierHtml, bioHtml, partyHtml) against the shared guard before extracting anything from it, mirroring the generic path's behavior.

3. Replace fetchCaOn()'s hardcoded `profile.leader_name = 'Doug Ford'` with a verified extraction using the already-built pickVerifiedName()/scoreNameCandidate() helpers from subnational-leader-profile-extract.cjs, so a real leadership change is detected (fetch would then fail loudly, as it already does for every other jurisdiction, rather than silently reporting a possibly-outdated hardcoded name forever).

4. Add a lightweight, reusable isBioTextSafe(text) export to the shared module so ANY future write path (including ones outside this pipeline entirely, like the federal member_bios mechanism) can validate text against the same pattern before writing, without needing to duplicate the regex.

5. Consider extending the existing client-side sanitizeBioText() guard in src/utils/mergeProvincialExplorerFirestore.js (already generic/jurisdiction-agnostic, applied at all 9 leader_bio/deputy_leader_bio read sites) to also run against whatever the federal member_bios render path uses, if that path is found to read raw Firestore text without a similar guard today.
